title: Air-fryer lemon pepper wings
subtitle: Crispy wings coated in lemon zest and cracked black pepper.
excerpt: Chicken wings coated in a mix of lemon zest, cracked black pepper, and garlic powder, then air-fried until blistered and crisp. The lemon brightens the seasoning without overpowering it. Serves two as a main or four as a snack.
sourceNotes: Lemon pepper seasoning is an American pantry blend used widely on chicken. This version uses fresh lemon zest for a more immediate citrus character than the dried commercial blend. The technique is a variation on the salt and pepper wing preparation.

content.text: Lemon pepper wings use fresh lemon zest rather than dried seasoning mix: the result is brighter and more fragrant. The zest goes on before cooking, not after, so it toasts slightly against the hot circulating air. Pat the wings dry before seasoning ,  wet skin stays soft.

items.prepNote: wing tips removed, patted completely dry

content.text: Pat {{chicken-wings}} of wings completely dry. Toss with the zest of {{lemon}} lemon, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt, {{garlic-powder}} of garlic powder, and a generous amount of cracked black pepper. Spray lightly with cooking oil. Preheat the air fryer to 200°C. Cook in a single layer for 12 minutes, flip, then cook for a further 10-13 minutes until golden and crisp. Squeeze the zested lemon over the wings before serving.

items.cause: Zest applied too lightly or the wings were wet.
items.fix: Use the zest of a whole lemon for 500 g of wings. Wet skin absorbs seasoning poorly ,  always dry first.
Cook in a single layer with space between pieces. Cook two batches rather than pile them in.
Zest only the coloured surface of the skin. Stop when you see white pith.

content.text: Lemon pepper wings are slightly fresher tasting than buffalo or barbecue versions. Good with a yoghurt and herb dip, or simply on their own as a quick snack. The same seasoning works on chicken thighs or drumsticks.
